Second pharma/healthcare name in the basket alongside BMY added sector correlation risk that didn't materialize into a shared drawdown today but should be tracked if a healthcare-wide move occurs; also a useful data point that 'freshness decay' on a catalyst is a real signal worth weighting more heavily in future sizing.

thesis: RSI 37.1, price below both SMAs with no negative news — a low-beta utility that sold off on flow, not fundamentals; targeting a partial reversion toward SMA20 (3.6% away).
outcome_notes: Price drifted up from $44.97 to $45.13, a small step toward SMA20 but the position was closed on schedule before the reversion could play out — the thesis direction was right but the move was too slow to capture the targeted 3.6% gap.
risks_observed: Low-beta utility kept realized P&L thin in both directions, masking whether the reversion edge is real or just noise; time-based exits on slow movers like this risk repeatedly harvesting fractions of the target and understating the strategy's true edge on this name class.

thesis: RSI 36.2 with no bad news and 5-day return already turning positive, suggesting the technical sell-off is stabilizing just below SMA20 (1.5% away).
outcome_notes: Price kept falling from $34.13 to the stop at $33.53 instead of stabilizing — the 5-day-return-turning-positive signal did not hold, and the stock breached the 1.5%-to-SMA20 zone that was supposed to cap the downside.
risks_observed: This is the falling-knife risk mean-reversion entries are exposed to: a short-term uptick in 5-day return isn't sufficient confirmation of a bottom, and 'no bad news' doesn't rule out a slow, newsless bleed; worth checking whether other baskets held correlated beaten-down names into the same risk-off tape, which would compound the stop-out.

thesis: Valero's Q2 beat both EPS (+24%) and sales (+14%) estimates, reported this morning, with refining margins boosted by the Iran-driven oil spike; the stock has pulled back 3% over the past week so the reaction is still fresh, not chased.

risks_observed: This entry shared its core driver (Iran-linked oil spike) and sector with the same-day SHEL trade, so the basket carried real energy/catalyst concentration even though only one leg worked; a reversal in crude on any de-escalation headline would have pressured both positions at once, and there's no evidence of an independent stop ahead of the take-profit trigger.

thesis: Shell's Q2 EPS more than doubled estimates and management announced a fresh $3B+ buyback extension same-day, a genuine capital-return catalyst in a sector the morning brief flags bullish on oil; sized smaller given the accompanying revenue miss.

The accompanying revenue miss likely capped any reaction, leaving the headline net-neutral for the market.
risks_observed: A flat outcome with cost drag suggests the catalyst was already priced in pre-market or was offset by the revenue miss — a signal worth screening for on future mixed-headline entries. At the basket level, this was the second same-day energy-sector position alongside VLO, so sector concentration risk was present even though this leg stayed inert rather than moving against the position.

thesis: Q2 EPS beat estimates by 24% and sales by 14%, filed today with price not yet reflecting the reaction; refining sector has genuine follow-through catalyst.

thesis: Q2 adj. EPS beat consensus by 123% and management announced a fresh $3B+ buyback today; energy sector tailwind from the brief supports follow-through.

thesis: H1 results drove the biggest dividend increase in years on strong copper free cash flow; market is still digesting yesterday's print with elevated volume.

thesis: Wells Fargo's PT raise to $500 with an 85%-upside call is fresh (yesterday) and volume-confirmed, though sized down since the stock already ran 11% over 20 days.

thesis: Financials are mildly bullish and confirmed by 5d sector strength (+1.12%); Visa's post-earnings beat with raised guidance and three analyst PT hikes ($410-430) is the cleanest expression of that call.

The 'mildly bullish' financials backdrop (+1.12% 5d) wasn't strong enough to cushion the pullback.

Single-name concentration in a mega-cap payments name also ties the trade to broad-market beta more than to the financials thesis specifically.

thesis: Health Care is this week's top-performing sector (5d +4.27%, mildly bullish macro call); Danaher shows the strongest relative strength (5d RS +10.1%) among the aligned candidates, holding above both SMAs.

Two macro-aligned sector picks (this and V) both stalled or reversed same-day, worth flagging as a basket-level pattern rather than isolated noise.

thesis: Q4 blowout (Azure +43% growth, $90B revenue) triggered a 9% premarket gap and a wave of analyst target hikes (Cantor to $522); sized modestly rather than maxed given this week's pattern of earnings-gap trades (GD, BCS, SMCI) fizzling flat by close, but the scale and breadth of sell-side re-rating here is a step above those setups.

risks_observed: The deliberately modest sizing (a defensive call against this week's fizzle pattern) capped upside on what turned out to be the strongest setup of the batch — a case where conservative sizing cost more in opportunity than it saved in risk. Basket-level correlation was still a live risk going in: four earnings-gap longs open in the same week meant a single macro or rates shock could have hit all of them simultaneously regardless of individual thesis quality, and the midday exit rule left no mechanism to let a genuine outlier like this one run further.

thesis: BP disclosed today it is putting its North Sea business up for sale alongside a 700-job cost-cutting plan — a fresh material event landing on top of last quarter's +22.1% earnings beat and a bullish energy sector tone, with reaction still fresh and Aug 4 earnings far enough away to avoid overlap.

A North Sea divestment plus job cuts is a slow-burn structural/cost story, not the kind of catalyst that typically moves a large-cap oil major intraday, so the flat tape is consistent with the market having already priced it in or shrugged it off.
risks_observed: Single-name concentration in a large integrated energy major with no idiosyncratic momentum on the day — the trade carried full sector/beta exposure to oil price and broader energy tone with no incremental edge from the news itself. Sitting flat into the Aug 4 earnings date (even though outside the holding window) is a reminder to sanity-check whether announcement-driven entries actually have a plausible intraday transmission mechanism before sizing them like momentum trades.

thesis: ML challenger: P(up)−P(down)=+0.79, predicted mild_up (+1.43%), hold 1d. Top features: vol_10d=+0.82, close_vs_sma21=+0.145, parkinson_10d=+0.0448
outcome_notes: Entry and exit prices were identical (0.84 to 0.84) — the predicted mild_up move simply never materialized, and the position closed on schedule with only cost drag as P&L. No evidence of the vol/trend signals translating into any intraday price action at all.

outcome_notes: Entry and exit both printed 14.17 — the highest-confidence, highest-magnitude call in the batch (predicted strong_up +4.27%) produced literally no price change, the worst calibration miss of the three trades.

thesis: Financials is Mildly Bullish and confirmed by relative strength (+2.10% 5d); BBVA's record profit, raised RoTE outlook, and $2.3B buyback give a fresh, clean-alignment catalyst.

thesis: Energy is the macro view's top-rated Bullish sector and today's news brief flags it as the lone risk-off bright spot; Shell's just-reported record Q2 earnings and cash generation are the stock-level catalyst.

As the day's lone risk-off bright spot, Energy exposure here is a single-sector bet on a fragile macro narrative; if broader risk sentiment had flipped, Shell's idiosyncratic earnings strength may not have been enough to offset basket-level correlation to risk assets.

thesis: RSI 32 and 12% below SMA20 with no bad news; sized smaller since below-average volume weakens confidence in an immediate reversal.
outcome_notes: Trade closed on the scheduled exit rather than hitting a defined profit or stop level, meaning the anticipated reversion off the 12%-below-SMA20 setup never materialized within the holding window — the position was flat-to-down and time simply ran out. Combined with IFX.DE, this was a second DACH-region loser on the same day under a 'transitional/mixed macro' tag — worth checking whether entries requiring 2+ days of continued coverage should be down-weighted or skipped versus fresher (T+0/T+1) disclosures.

thesis: Record Q3 revenue and an AI-demand-driven guidance raise to ~$18.8B FY revenue landed yesterday; stock is still below both SMAs with only 1.01x volume, meaning the re-rating is still developing, not exhausted.

risks_observed: The 'above both SMAs' trend signal offered no protection against a same-day reversal — a purely fundamentals-driven entry with no volume or momentum confirmation at time of trade, and no secondary catalyst to fall back on when the price didn't cooperate.

thesis: +14.3% earnings surprise released this morning plus fresh UniCredit-dialogue headlines add M&A speculation on top of the fundamental beat.

thesis: Bayer's CropScience Q2 beat (seed profit tops forecasts), a lowered debt forecast, and a Supreme Court litigation win are three independent positive catalysts from the last 48 hours. thesis: Financials are Mildly Bullish in the macro view and confirmed by sector strength (XLF +2.33% 5d); SAN.MC's 5d pace (+6.71%, ~1.3%/day) is accelerating versus its 20d pace, with RSI 65 and a clean breakout above both SMAs, and its low 0.30% round-trip cost is the only aligned name whose realistic momentum clears the cost gate.

Both trades exited on schedule rather than a stop, so there's no evidence a protective exit would have triggered before scheduled close — worth checking whether intraday drawdown on SAN.MC exceeded what a stop-loss would have caught.

Worth reviewing whether 'freshness of disclosure' should carry more weight than the blanket regime discount in sizing.

thesis: H1 earnings beat with upgraded full-year guidance drove a volume-confirmed (2.24x) breakout above both MAs; highest conviction of the set.

Volume-confirmed breakouts on beat-and-raise news can still be sold into once early buyers take profit; the earnings pop looks to have been the top, not the start of a trend.
risks_observed: This was tagged the highest-conviction setup of the set yet was the day's only loser — a reminder that conviction ranking doesn't correlate with outcome and shouldn't drive oversized allocation. No secondary confirmation (e.g., waiting for a pullback/hold above the breakout level) was required before entry, which would have avoided chasing the initial earnings spike.

thesis: Harbour Energy's Q2 print showed record H1 production and raised full-year free cash flow guidance, landing alongside a Hormuz-driven Brent rally that adds a sector tailwind to a genuine earnings beat.

risks_observed: A meaningful chunk of the move was macro (oil), not stock-specific — the Hormuz headline risk could just as easily have reversed intraday and erased the gain before the take-profit level was hit. Sector correlation (energy) means this wasn't a pure idiosyncratic-earnings win.

thesis: Apollo signed a definitive £5.7bn/$7.7bn takeover of easyJet today, confirmed by multiple sources with 2.95x volume — the 5-day move (+7.87%) looks like only partial convergence toward deal value, leaving room to run with residual bidding-war optionality (Castlelake was the rival bidder).

risks_observed: Late entry into a deal-arb situation caps near-term upside once most of the premium is priced, while leaving full binary downside exposure if Apollo's deal had wobbled or Castlelake failed to counter — none of that tail risk is visible in a near-zero P&L print.

Basket-level: this and VUL.L both closed the same session on European/UK oversold setups — worth checking whether the two were driven by a shared regional risk-off/on move rather than independent stock-specific dips.

thesis: RSI 6.7 with below-average volume — the decline shows no capitulation spike, consistent with a technical drift oversold rather than a fundamentally-driven selloff.
outcome_notes: The 7% reversion off an RSI of 6.7 played out fast, hitting take-profit by midday with no capitulation volume at entry — supports the thesis that this was drift-oversold exhaustion rather than a fundamental repricing. Move size is large for a single-session mean-reversion and outpaced the TKBP.SW trade, suggesting either a thinner order book or a sharper snapback than the entry model priced in.
risks_observed: Below-average volume at entry is a liquidity flag on a UK small/mid-cap — wider spreads or a thin book could exaggerate both the entry fill and the exit price, inflating the realized 7% versus what's achievable at size. An RSI this extreme (6.7) is itself a hindsight signal worth flagging: it's rare enough that it may warrant a secondary sanity check (e.g., confirming no halted/illiquid print) before sizing up on similarly extreme readings going forward.

Worth checking whether AUCO.L (also filled today) added correlated sector exposure on top of this.

risks_observed: Single-name exposure on the DAX with no stated catalyst means the move could reverse as quickly as it built if it was driven by short-term momentum flow rather than news; the midday take-profit exit also means there's no visibility into whether the breakout extended further into the close, which is worth tracking to calibrate the take-profit threshold.

thesis: Heaviest volume breakout in the set (4.63x) above rising MAs; sized moderately since AUCP.L/AUCO.AS are the same underlying exposure.

Combined with WPM.L's metals-rally exposure, today's basket may have carried more sector/theme concentration in precious metals than the per-trade sizing suggests.

thesis: Materials is the #2 sector this week (+4.82% 5d) and directly confirmed by the precious-metals surge in the macro view; RIO's 3.02x volume spike on a clean MACD/SMA uptrend signals real institutional participation, not just drift.

thesis: 56.2% earnings surprise with price still drifting up on light volume — genuine post-earnings drift still developing, not a spent buzz pop.

risks_observed: Drift theses need more runway than this strategy's scheduled exit gives them; a near-zero move that eats the full holding period without triggering either exit is a silent cost (time/opportunity risk) not flagged by P&L alone.

thesis: 35.6% earnings beat confirmed by peer results (Loar, Ducommun) in a bullish defence/aerospace tape, RSI not yet overbought.

risks_observed: Directly correlated with the RR.L trade (same defence/aerospace bucket, same day, same stop outcome) — this is the basket-level risk that materialized: a sector-wide reversal hit both positions rather than one stock-specific miss, and the basket had no cross-position exposure cap to catch it.

thesis: $10.1B profit beat and restarted $1B buyback are a fresh, confirmed catalyst with heavy volume confirmation; RSI 53.8 leaves room to run.

risks_observed: Second bank name in the basket alongside CBK.DE — sector concentration didn't hurt today but the two names diverged in outcome, showing the earnings-beat setup isn't uniformly reliable even within the same sector on the same day.

thesis: Buybacks, dividend increase and multiple analyst target upgrades are a live catalyst still being priced in, with only a modest 5d move so far.

thesis: STM's +56.2% earnings surprise (2026-08-03) is driving a multi-day post-earnings drift with MACD histogram turning positive; sized modestly since below-average volume today suggests the initial pop has partly cooled.

thesis: $10.1B profit beat restarts a $1B buyback plus another interim dividend, confirmed on 3.7x average volume — a clean, still-fresh catalyst rather than stale news.
